name: Lateral Lunge
description: The lateral lunge steps to the side rather than forward or backward, loading the working leg in the frontal plane and providing a unique training stimulus for the adductors, gluteus medius, and quadriceps simultaneously. The inner thigh of the stationary leg is stretched while the working leg squats. It develops frontal-plane strength and mobility that forward/backward lunges do not address.

execution.starting_position: Stand with feet together, core engaged, hands on hips or holding dumbbells at the sides.
execution.setup_instructions: Wear footwear with good lateral grip. Perform bodyweight first to establish the movement pattern before adding load.
steps: Step 1: Take a large step directly to one side — the foot lands flat and pointed forward or slightly outward.
Step 2: Sit the hip of the stepping leg back and down, bending that knee while keeping the stationary leg straight.
Step 3: Keep the torso relatively upright and reach the hands forward or keep them on the hips for balance.
Step 4: Drive through the working heel to push back to the starting position.
Step 5: Alternate sides each rep or complete all reps on one side.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale as you step out and lower. Exhale as you return to standing.
common_mistakes: Taking too small a step, reducing the adductor stretch and hip loading
Letting the working knee cave inward
Excessive forward lean of the torso
safety_considerations: Adequate hip adductor flexibility is necessary — start with a shorter step and increase gradually
If adductor soreness is severe the day after, reduce step width in the next session
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: The working knee bends until the thigh approaches parallel. The stationary leg stays straight with the foot flat.
coaching_cues: Sit back into the hip, not down onto the knee
Keep the stationary leg long and straight
Foot flat on the working leg — don't let the heel rise
